reason: Contract section 6: 'a required field is missing'. This record has no track_id, so Consumer 1 could not key track-activity even if it wanted to.
Contract section 6: 'event_type is not "play"'. v1 carries plays only -- CD-1 deliberately excludes save, follow and playlist_add -- so a skip event has no place on play-events.
Contract section 6: 'an ID is empty'. listener_id is also the play-events partition key, so an empty one would produce an unkeyed record and break Consumer 1's per-listener state (CD-3).
Contract section 6: 'played_seconds is negative'. A negative listen duration is not a short play, it is a corrupt one, and it would skew any band-share denominator it landed in.

Contract section 6: 'played_seconds is greater than track_duration_seconds'. This is the contract's own worked invalid example. It is the only rule enforced by a model-level validator rather than a field constraint, so the rejection carries the model's own 'exceeds' wording.

Contract section 6: 'track_duration_seconds is not positive'. A zero-length track makes the played-within-duration rule vacuous and would divide by zero in any completion-rate metric built on it later.

Contract section 6: 'event_time is not a valid UTC timestamp'. A space instead of the 'T' and no trailing 'Z' -- every window in this project is measured on event_time (CD-7), so an unparseable one is not a cosmetic defect.

Not a section 6 bullet but the same class of defect: PlayEventV1 sets extra='forbid', so a field outside the 9-field contract is rejected rather than silently ignored. country_code is the specific field CD-1 excluded from v1, which is exactly the one a well-meaning producer change would add back.

Contract section 6: 'the Kafka key does not equal the value's listener_id'. The record itself is entirely valid and the model is right to accept it -- PlayEventV1 validates the Kafka value and never sees the key, so no validator on it could ever compare the two. Consumer 1 must assert this explicitly with key_matches_listener_id. Here a record whose value says FA01 arrives under the key FL01, which would route one listener's plays into another listener's per-listener state.
